notes.title: **USB AUDIO 10 CH FX**
notes.text: **USB AUDIO 10 CH FX** (owner 2026-10-26: "8 mono + stereo FX give full mix control"): MENU > USB AUDIO is 2 CH / 10 CH MIX (channels 1-2 the master, the 10 CH before) / 10 CH FX (channels 1-2 the chorus, delay and reverb buses' return, mono on both, at the MASTER level, before PERFORM's master effects, METRO and the master chain). T1..T8 panned + the FX pair = the master bus before its chain (18 LSB in the test). MIX <-> FX: no reconnect, a 5.8 ms cross-fade. Saved in the palette word's bits 12..13 (e586073's 10 CH reads as MIX). The 10 CH device's channels 1-2 are named Main L / R now (bcdDevice 3.82). Standard build only.

notes.title: **USB AUDIO 2 CH / 10 CH**
notes.text: **USB AUDIO 2 CH / 10 CH** (MENU, hold HOME; the owner's 8-track test build of 2026-10-26, "that works"): 10 CH sends the master L R and the eight tracks T1..T8 (mono, each before PAN, the sends and the master's effects) to the computer as a 10-channel USB audio input ("Hortator 8ch", 16-bit 44.1 kHz, 920 B packets); 2 CH (the default) is the stereo master as before, byte for byte the same USB device. The change applies when the menu closes: the FM-1 leaves USB for 1 s and comes back as the other device, the sequencer and the sound playing on (CLK USB: the steps wait for the clock up to 2 s after it). Saved in the settings record (the palette word's bit 12; older records: 2 CH). SAFE START is always 2 CH. The app's USB driver is usb_app8.c: the frozen usb_app.c plus marked insertions only (tools/check_usb_fork.py); in 10 CH its 920 B packet is queued from every TIMER5 tick (10 kHz): at 2 kHz the test build lost ~10 % of the frames (tears). 10 CH needs the standard, non-Bluetooth build (owner 2026-10-26): the Bluetooth build has no USB AUDIO row, is always 2 CH and ignores a stored 10 CH (its RAM, 85868 of 98304 B, would have been 97644 B); its binary is the same as 0.24.0's.

notes.title: Web site only
notes.text: Web site only: the landing page has a manual before the engines: a map of the panel (point at a control on a small FM-1, or at its line, to see what it does) and ten short guides (find your way, make a beat, shape a sound, play and record live, mute, perform, lock a step, save and chain, MIDI and LEARN, settings). Manual in the top bar and the footer; More below leads to it.
